key: The raw, whose mass hath not been heated gains not this: they only which are dressed, which bear, attain to it.
s: Opening a hymn that hails Brahmanaspati’s filter, the verse sets the raw against the dressed; Sāyaṇa, on 9.83.1, reads the raw as one whose body no milk vow or like observance has heated, and the dressed who bear as the ripened, carrying the sacrifice through.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.83.1, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.८३, revision 322742 (2021)

evidence.words: तव “तत् पवित्रम् "अतप्ततनूः पयोव्रतादिना असंतप्तगात्रः "आमः अपरिपक्वो "न “अश्नुते न व्याप्नोति । “शृतास "इत् शृता एवं परिपक्वा एव "वहन्तः यागं निर्वहन्तः “तत् पवित्रं "समाशत व्याप्नुवन्ति ।
evidence.gloss: That filter of yours the one whose body is unheated, whose limbs have not been heated by the milk vow and the like, the raw, the unripe, does not reach. The dressed (śṛtāsaḥ): only those thus ripened (paripakvāḥ); bearing (vahantaḥ): carrying the sacrifice through (yāgaṃ nirvahantaḥ); they reach that filter.

reason: Problem holds: the sentence gave ‘the dressed’ the gloss Sāyaṇa gives ‘which bear’. Re-opened packet.js veda 99 --verse 9.83.1: he glosses śṛtāsaḥ as śṛtā evaṃ paripakvā eva (only those thus ripened) and vahantaḥ separately as yāgaṃ nirvahantaḥ (carrying the sacrifice through). Changed only the reading’s second limb, to ‘the dressed who bear as the ripened, carrying the sacrifice through’, so each gloss sits on its own word; the fix’s ‘those so ripened who carry’ ran to 46 words, so ‘so’ and the second relative were cut (the ripening by the observances just named is carried by the first limb). Key, plain sense, commentator and source unchanged. verse.js ok (9.83.1, [805,1]); entry-check ok on scratch/V-d099-p.json.
